text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - The FTSE 100 finished almost unchanged after a late U.S-inspired rally bucked up prices depressed earlier by fears over interest rate rises after the latest domestic inflation figures. The FTSE 100 finished off just 0.8 points at 3,926.1 after an erratic session which saw shares hit lows of 3,904.

FRANKFURT - Shares shrugged off an early bout of profit-taking to end bourse trade slightly higher, boosted by gains in the banking sector and continuing a rally begun on Tuesday. The blue-chip DAX index touched an all-time bourse high of 2,785.16 points in early dealings, then pared gains. The DAX index ended bourse trade up 3.58 points at 2,777.01 points and was mostly steady at 2,784.39 in post-bourse IBIS electronic trading.

PARIS - Stocks closed barely higher after briefly touching a new year high in a day of very heavy trading which saw frenetic action in shares of insurers UAP and Axa. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 0.99 points or 0.04 percent at 2218.18.

ZURICH - Shares set a new record closing high after an early boost in the financial sector and a late dollar rally pushed prices ahead. Dealers said investor interest was focused on financials, cyclicals and consumer stocks. The broad SPI index finished 19.66 points higher at 2,463.63.

TOKYO - Stocks ended slightly higher. Participants remained sidelined as even a slew of corporate earnings results failed to serve as an incentive, brokers said, adding that the government's package of financial deregulation measures would take time to implement. The key Nikkei 225 average gained 51.60 points, or 0.25 percent, to close at 21,031.04.

HONG KONG - The Hang Seng Index closed above 13,000 points for the first time ever, driven by optimism about interest rates and the property market. The index closed 61.11 points higher at 13,004.80 after hitting a record intraday high at 13,009.74.

SYDNEY - Shares had a more buoyant session as gold and other metal sectors found plenty of buying support after base and precious metal prices edged higher on Wednesday. The All Ordinaries index closed up 15.6 points at 2,362.5, just off its intra-day higher of 2,365.4.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares ramped up in busy dealings on perceptions the heavy selling, which has wiped almost three percent off the market's value this month, was overdone. Dealers said buyers were lured into the market during the morning when it became evident futures players, who have been responsible for large-volume arbitrage sales, were keeping largely to the sidelines. The overall index ended 60.6 points firmer at 6,815.9 supported by the industrial index which rose 66.1 points to 7,980.2 and the gold index up 31.7 points at 1,743.6.
